summary.message: PostgreSQL and Redis audited successfully. Neo4j unreachable (missing credentials). Qdrant not tested (vector DB, no direct SQL audit applicable). PostgreSQL has CRITICAL security gaps: superuser-only access with default password, no RLS, no triggers, 19 unindexed foreign keys. Redis has no authentication configured.

tables: ALL PRIVILEGES on all public tables

issues: Application connects as superuser 'postgres' — violates least-privilege principle
Default password 'postgres' in use — trivially guessable
Superuser bypasses all access controls including RLS
No separate application role exists — no privilege separation

tables: ALL PRIVILEGES on all public tables

issues: Developer account has SUPERUSER + BYPASSRLS + REPLICATION — maximum privileges
Acceptable for local development only, must not exist in production
RLS is NOT enabled on any table despite migration 009_rls_policies.py existing
All data is accessible to any authenticated database connection with no row-level filtering
Sensitive tables (users, payments, chat_messages) have zero row isolation
CRITICAL: Only superuser roles exist — no application-level role with restricted privileges
CRITICAL: Default password 'postgres' used for database connection
CRITICAL: No RLS policies active despite migration file existing
No read-only role for reporting/analytics
No separate role for migration operations
recommendations: Create a dedicated 'groupio_app' role with only INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE on public tables
Create a 'groupio_readonly' role for analytics and debugging
Change the postgres password to a strong, generated value
Enable RLS on sensitive tables (users, payments, chat_messages, audit_logs)
Run the existing RLS migration (009_rls_policies.py) or apply manually
Revoke superuser from all application connections

constraints: NOT NULL: email, hashed_password, full_name, phone, role
DEFAULT: is_active=true, is_verified=false, preferred_language='he', created_at=now(), updated_at=now()
issues: Column is 'hashed_password' not 'password_hash' — code/test mismatch detected
No updated_at auto-update trigger — application must set manually on every UPDATE
No audit trail trigger for user modifications

constraints: NOT NULL: name, address, city, region, created_at, updated_at
issues: FK column admin_user_id has no index — JOINs will full-scan
No updated_at auto-update trigger
audit_logs itself can be deleted — no protection for audit trail integrity
No immutability constraint (should be append-only)
No triggers exist to auto-update 'updated_at' timestamps — all UPDATE operations must set this in application code
No triggers exist for audit logging — all audit entries must be explicitly created by the application
Audit logs table is writable (UPDATE/DELETE) — should be append-only in production
Column naming inconsistency: code references 'password_hash' but DB column is 'hashed_password'
recommendations: Create a trigger function to auto-set updated_at on UPDATE for all tables that have the column
Make audit_logs table append-only (REVOKE UPDATE, DELETE on audit_logs FROM app role)
Standardize column naming between code and database schema

issues: ZERO triggers defined in the entire database
No auto-update triggers for updated_at columns
No audit/logging triggers
No data validation triggers
No cascade/business logic triggers
Functions exist (archive_old_chat_messages, join_offer_atomic) but are not invoked via triggers

functions_found.name: archive_old_chat_messages
functions_found.purpose: Archives old chat messages (must be called manually or via cron/scheduler)

functions_found.name: join_offer_atomic
functions_found.args: p_id varchar, p_offer_id varchar, p_user_id varchar, p_unit_count integer
functions_found.purpose: Atomic offer join operation with participant count increment

recommendations: Create updated_at trigger: CREATE FUNCTION set_updated_at() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$ BEGIN NEW.updated_at = NOW(); RETURN NEW; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql; then attach to all tables with updated_at column
Consider audit triggers on users, payments, and offers tables for compliance
Schedule archive_old_chat_messages via pg_cron or application scheduler

performance_notes: PK index on id, unique indexes on email and phone

All users have onboarded_at=NULL — onboarding tracking not active

issues: All 6 offers are 'pending' with 0 participants — no active marketplace data
pricing_rationale is NULL for all offers — AI pricing not invoked
Empty — no participants have joined any offers
Empty — no contractor profiles exist despite a contractor user existing in users table
Empty — no payments recorded
Empty — no invoices generated
Migration 019 applied — schema is up to date
19 foreign key columns lack indexes — JOINs on these columns will cause sequential scans

Data is minimal (demo/seed level) — not representative of production load
recommendations: Create indexes on all 19 unindexed FK columns — critical for query performance at scale
Add triggers or application logic to keep denormalized counters in sync
Ensure contractor user creation flow also creates the contractors table record
Run ANALYZE after bulk data changes to update query planner statistics

top_findings: CRITICAL: Application connects as PostgreSQL superuser with default password 'postgres'
CRITICAL: No Row-Level Security (RLS) enabled — any DB connection sees all data
CRITICAL: Zero triggers in entire database — no automated data integrity enforcement
HIGH: 19 foreign key columns lack indexes — will cause full table scans at scale
HIGH: No updated_at auto-update mechanism — relies entirely on application code
HIGH: Audit logs table allows UPDATE/DELETE — audit trail is mutable
MEDIUM: Counter columns (resident_count, active_offers) out of sync with actual data
MEDIUM: Contractor user has no corresponding contractors record — referential gap
MEDIUM: No separate application role — only superuser roles exist
LOW: All user.last_login values are NULL — login tracking not functioning
recommended_actions: 1. IMMEDIATE: Change postgres password from default 'postgres' to a strong generated value
2. IMMEDIATE: Create a dedicated application role with minimum required privileges
3. HIGH: Create indexes on all 19 unindexed foreign key columns
4. HIGH: Create updated_at trigger function and attach to all tables with that column
5. HIGH: Enable RLS on users, payments, chat_messages, audit_logs tables
6. MEDIUM: Make audit_logs table append-only (revoke UPDATE/DELETE from app role)
7. MEDIUM: Add triggers to maintain denormalized counters (resident_count, active_offers)
8. MEDIUM: Fix contractor user creation flow to also create contractors profile
9. LOW: Populate last_login on successful authentication

issues: CRITICAL: No password required (requirepass not set)
CRITICAL: protected-mode is OFF and bound to all interfaces (* -::*)
Any client on the network can read/write/flush all data
Refresh tokens and email verification tokens are exposed without authentication
CRITICAL: Redis has no authentication — anyone on the network can access all data
CRITICAL: Protected mode is disabled AND binding to all interfaces
Refresh tokens stored in plaintext without authentication
No ACL rules defined beyond the default user
recommendations: Set requirepass to a strong password in redis.conf
Enable protected-mode
Bind to 127.0.0.1 only (or use firewall rules)
Create separate ACL users for the application with limited command access
Consider encrypting sensitive tokens at rest

issues: Redis does not support triggers — keyspace notifications may be configured for pub/sub
Email verification tokens expire correctly (TTL ~11 hours)
Refresh tokens have ~6.4 day TTL — matches REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS=7 config
4 refresh tokens active for what appears to be 4 users — expected
Only 6 keys total — minimal operational data
No rate limiting keys present (rate:*, auth_ip:*) — rate limiting may not be active
No agent state or cache keys — features may not be exercised
recommendations: Verify rate limiting is functioning by checking for rate:* keys during API usage
Monitor memory usage as key count grows — currently 1.19MB with noeviction policy

issues: AOF (Append-Only File) is disabled — in a crash, up to the last RDB snapshot of data could be lost
For auth tokens this is acceptable (users re-login), but consider enabling AOF for production

top_findings: CRITICAL: No authentication — Redis is wide open to any network client
CRITICAL: Protected mode OFF + bound to all interfaces
HIGH: Refresh tokens stored without database-level access control
MEDIUM: AOF persistence disabled — potential token loss on crash
LOW: No rate limiting keys observed — feature may be inactive
recommended_actions: 1. IMMEDIATE: Set requirepass in Redis configuration
2. IMMEDIATE: Bind Redis to 127.0.0.1 or use network-level ACLs
4. HIGH: Create application-specific ACL user with limited commands
5. MEDIUM: Enable AOF persistence for production deployment
6. LOW: Verify rate limiting is operational

global_recommendations: CRITICAL: Implement authentication on ALL databases — PostgreSQL (change default password), Redis (set requirepass), Qdrant (set API key), Neo4j (configure password)
CRITICAL: Create dedicated application database roles with minimum privileges — stop using superuser for application connections
CRITICAL: Enable Row-Level Security on PostgreSQL for multi-tenant data isolation
HIGH: Create 19 missing FK indexes in PostgreSQL to prevent full table scans
HIGH: Implement updated_at trigger function across all PostgreSQL tables
HIGH: Bind all databases to localhost or use network-level ACLs — do not expose on 0.0.0.0
MEDIUM: Make audit_logs table immutable (append-only) by revoking UPDATE/DELETE from application role
MEDIUM: Enable Redis AOF persistence for production
MEDIUM: Fix data integrity gaps — contractor profiles, counter sync, last_login tracking
LOW: Document database architecture, connection strings, and backup/restore procedures
LOW: Set up database monitoring (connection pool usage, slow queries, disk usage)

errors.resolution: Set NEO4J_PASSWORD in .env and re-run audit
